name: Chrome in the Water: Illegal Augmentation Trials, 2181-2193
description: Assembled from medical waste records, pirated surgical logs, and the testimonies of seventeen survivors, this underground documentary chronicles a decade of unlicensed chrome augmentation trials conducted on the Gray Zone residents through contaminated water-soluble delivery systems — meaning subjects never knew they were being augmented until hardware began presenting through their skin. The film was compiled by a collective of three journalists working under the shared pseudonym Isadora Null; one of the three was killed before the film's completion, their section finished by the remaining two from their notes. The film circulates exclusively on degradable physical chips designed to self-erase after three viewings.
cultural_impact: The self-erasing chip format became a model for subsequent underground documentary distribution and is now called 'Null format' after the collective's pseudonym.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone resident begins presenting chrome hardware through their skin twenty years after the trial period — their body has been slowly metabolizing a delayed-activation augmentation payload.

One of the surviving journalists from the Isadora Null collective is now living as a licensed Tier 3 citizen under a new identity and is terrified that the film's renewed circulation will expose them.
The 'Cascade contractor' named obliquely in the film is a subsidiary that still operates — under a different name — and is currently bidding on a new the Gray Zone water infrastructure contract.
